rationale: Final source step for the active Candidate 0922502bc12a4af68ee74cb77942fd72 before the run's time boundary: narrowing the disjoint-slow-quorum scenario to its actual precondition. For even N, a recovery that rebuilds from a non-majority slow quorum can only produce a conflicting outcome if the recovering replica reaches the recovery path for the instance without holding its committed value. handleCommit sets the instance to COMMITTED with the committed command for every replica that receives the broadcast, and startRecoveryForInstance returns early when inst.Status >= COMMITTED and inst.Cmds != nil (epaxos/epaxos.go:1127-1135), so a replica that received the Commit cannot be the one that restarts the instance. The broadcast itself is gated on liveness: bcastCommit iterates PreferredPeerOrder and skips peers with !r.Alive (epaxos/epaxos.go:579-600), and crtInstance only advances together with creating an instance entry, so the missing-Commit precondition requires a replica that learned of the instance (or of the row position) while the commit was skipped for it - a membership/liveness condition rather than a message reordering. That is a different activity (A4) from the quorum arithmetic, so I record it here as the narrowed remaining premise instead of claiming a defect. The confirmed durability finding is unaffected. Time boundary reached without a new obligation for this question; nothing is asserted about whether such a replica can exist.

Since bcastCommit skips non-Alive peers, that precondition is a liveness/membership condition rather than a consequence of the quorum sizes alone.
